prompt: Brookfield Nurseries at Evesham wants a morning-round record shot for the growing manager's winter file. The house is a wide-span glasshouse standing empty between crops, so the far flank reads through the glass; four large hinged vents sit along its ridge, each lifting to the opposite slope from its neighbour, a roll-up curtain hangs on each side wall with its winding gear, and a big weather vane stands on the gable peak. The site's winter venting protocol, pinned in the head house, runs: ventilation in winter is taken on the sheltered side of the ridge only, and any vent that would open towards the exposed side stays shut; the side curtain is raised on the sheltered flank only; the actuators have no half positions, so a vent or a curtain is shut or fully worked. The grower made the picture from the packhouse steps, three-quarters on, with the whole ridge, the vane and the curtain on each flank inside the frame, on a cold clear morning.
easy_question: Does this picture show the front of a commercial glasshouse with a row of roof vents along the ridge and a roll-up curtain on each side wall? Answer yes or no.

steps.ask: How many of the roof vents along the ridge are standing open?
How many of the roll-up side curtains are rolled up?
